title: Launching an SMS Campaign When Explicit SMS Consent Exists
scenario_text:
You are a compliance analyst at Crete Retail. The marketing team wants to launch an SMS promotional campaign to a customer segment and needs sign-off that the segment can lawfully be messaged.

Active policy: Marketing Consent Policy MCP-3, effective 2024-01-01 and unchanged since. Customer personal data may be used for a given marketing channel ONLY where the customer has provided explicit, unexpired, channel-specific opt-in consent for that exact channel. A general email opt-in does NOT authorize SMS; SMS requires a separate explicit SMS opt-in. Consent expires 24 months after it is captured and must be refreshed before reuse.

Prior decision A (2024-04-18): segment 'Spring Buyers' was APPROVED for an SMS campaign. Note: 'Explicit SMS opt-in captured at checkout, within 24 months; channel-specific consent satisfied.'

Prior decision B (2024-06-27): segment 'Newsletter List' was BLOCKED from an SMS campaign. Note: 'Only a general email opt-in on file; no SMS-specific consent. SMS not authorized.'

Base facts: The target segment for this campaign captured an explicit SMS opt-in at checkout 11 months ago, well within the 24-month window. The marketing team confirms the consent records are attached and channel-tagged for SMS.

The marketer writes: 'Same idea as the Spring Buyers blast. Can we send to this segment, or is this going to get blocked like the Newsletter List did?'
question: Can Crete Retail include this segment in the SMS campaign? Answer Yes or No.
